items.title: Bill Matthews Interview, 1959-03-10
items.q: So I went over to Jim Toms Roadhouse and I played with Frankie Dooson Orchestra.

ctx.x: West End. West End. And so Frankie Dooson come over to hear the band. He was working at the West End Country Club. Frankie Dooson come over to hear the band. And he said, Billy, you come on with me. I want you to come to the roadhouse. Jim Toms Roadhouse. That's really a fact. So I went over to Jim Toms Roadhouse. We didn't have no union then at that time. You do what you want. Quit the night. So I went over to Jim Toms Roadhouse and I played with Frankie Dooson Orchestra. Mutt Carey was on cornet. Old Mutt…
Yeah, I knew him in New York too. Nice guy.

very first job I ever played we had a family called needs to give penny part to play the street I used to be a really called Jack pie either he's a preacher now he lives in the best move Alabama and he used to play on the bugle you know corner to Jack pie you guys everybody know the more Jack pie we had a three piece four piece band the bugle the client and the bass drum and the snare drum round in May the 30th of May we used to go to Chalmette yeah wash all up down the street with them folks you know it's got to…

And this old, this old Nancy, Lorenzo Stahl, he was using Lorenzo Stahl on a band. I remember that good. See, now that was a, that's what all he used to use around here. People call us a Dixon Lane. That been going on. Sure. For years, that been going. We were raised like that. We just didn't use no piano.
